source.text: The largest volume-mean fuel temperature of any slice: the volume-mean fuel temperature of a slice, the surface temperature plus 1/2 of the centre-to-surface rise (the solid cylinder's parabola), from the closed-form solution of each slice at its own heat rate and coolant. The power shape is a cosine, normalised to an average of 1 (the slice at the middle has (pi/2) cos(0) = 1.571 of the average). The tolerance is the sum of the three terms of the peak entries of this case, each fixed before any run (the mesh term 5 x rise / 100^2 is for a cell-centre value; a volume mean of the cells is less sensitive to the mesh, so it is conservative here), taken at its largest over the slices: 5 K (including the axial conduction allowance of 3 x 0.00099 x 1154.9 K and the cosine's 41-point table), rounded up to 0.05 K.
source.check: Second method: FEED's closed form of each slice integrated over the fuel cross-section (Simpson, tests/seedFuelTemperature.test.ts), the same means worked by hand in tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, and the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1): the solver's cell-weighted means are inside the tolerance.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin (constant conductivities, convective boundary 573 K and 30000 W/m2/K on every slice) as 9 radial slices over 0.381 m with a cosine power shape, 20 kW/m on average (31.4 kW/m at the peak)
